venues.name: D&C Denver
venues.narrative: **DVR — Sunday 11/22 (AM & PM MOD Maggie H; entered by MJH; posted 1:31am ET 11/23)** Net $7,260.39 vs target $5,580 (130.1%; form notes +$1,681). No events — the 'including events' fields were entered as NA, so Total Net Sales is used. AM (coffee) $1,531.95, D&C PM $5,728.44, Garden/6A n/a. Food $1,843.90. Comps $398.27 (5.5%). 181 guests (Tock); check avg $40.11 (net / guests). AM: first solo shift for the opener — a pretty busy Sunday with lots of cocktails and a constant flow from 7:30 onward; low on cold brew and none got brewed today. Big shout-out to Hiram for a $1,500 solo shift. PM: sleepy all night until 9pm, then the pops hit. Several team members' families were in. JP held down the door through the rushes, stayed on top of bussing and even took some orders; Graham, Mel and Daunte kept ticket times a non-issue behind the bar. Several staff sounding under the weather — MOD asked everyone to rest and hydrate. Kitchen: chill and somewhat steady Sunday for Fiellah, Marv and the closing chef; a bit more prep than usual tomorrow. Caviar 86'd unless more arrives tomorrow; 4 orders of rabbit left. 911: walnut cilantro pesto, roasted fingerlings, poppy seed vinaigrette, honey butter quenelles, toasted panko crumbs. Low: chicken thighs in brine, fried garlic, chicken breast butterflies, cocktail sauce, spinach artichoke dip, wagyu flanks, cookie dough. Break make-up complete. No incidents; no-shows not charged. Highlight: former GM Shelley in for an 11pm reservation.

venues.name: D&C East Village
venues.weather: Sporadic rain hurt us fo sho
venues.narrative: **EV — Sunday 11/22 (MOD Kyler, Chef Michael; entered by Thomas; posted 1:33am ET 11/23)** Net $4,370 vs target $4,566 (95.7%). Food $453, beverage $3,917; no events. Comps $63.78 (1.5%) — a couple of shots plus investor discount. 115 covers (Sevenrooms); check avg $38. Sporadic rain hurt the night. Breezy opening build of pre- and post-dinner guests with a chatty energy. Two musicians from a touring band stopped in and ran up over $200 in martinis. Right before 11 a Thanksgiving-break crowd gave the room a resurgence, but it vanished quickly — only two covers after 11pm. Back-catalog banger: Saga, for a Toronto guest who frequents fine dining but was new to cocktails. 5 large parties (all fives), 6 solos. Top sellers: High Plains Drifter, Shinebox, Rosalie, Burner Phone. Door: very chill night with a solid 6pm start; avoided a waitlist entirely and may have hit capacity around 7. A couple who got engaged today came in to celebrate because their first date was here. No no-shows. Menu count 19; breakage 1 wine glass.

venues.name: D&C Los Angeles
venues.narrative: **LA — Sunday 11/22 (MOD Julian, Chef Angel; entered by Julian Catano; posted 3:26am ET 11/23)** Net $4,240 vs target $5,040 (84.1%). Food $761; Marquee $4,240 (food $761); Standing Room $0; no events. Comps $112 (2.6%) — DNL, service recovery, discounts. 122 guests; check avg $34.76. Started super chill, enough for one server to run the floor. Guests rolled in mid-service, leading to a full house and full bar for a while, even a waitlist. Died out in the later hours once it started raining. Round one of the new drink menu tasting ran 2–5pm, with a lot of information on the new drinks. Overall a chill shift (the form says 'for a Monday' — it was Sunday), with a handful of large parties and new guests checking out the spot. Kitchen: two-man crew sending food out quickly; all good with the team. Maintenance: oven still down. 86'd/low: Hallow Technique, Contrabandista, Shinebox (new menu flip). No incidents; no-shows charged. Highlight: trying the new drinks for fall and winter.

Note: Marquee bar sales and 'Total Sales' were both entered as $3,566.75, which is $846.52 above the net figure with comps reported as 0 — the gap is unexplained on the form; the net-including-events field is used per convention. Garden closed. Food $235; no events. Comps: 0; voids 1% (86'd items). 61 guests (43 walk-ins, 18 reservations); guest avg $41.85 and check avg $115.09 as reported. D&C: busy, inventory-filled day; slow start, decent pop in the middle, tapered off to an easy close. Kitchen: slow night; kitchen close not checked. Went well: teamwork, Season's Greetings decor. Do better: foot traffic. No incidents; no-shows not charged; $0 no-show revenue. Maintenance: curtains, hot water. Highlight: newbie chartreuse lovers.

venues.name: Municipal Grand F&B
venues.weather: overcast and balmy but no rain!
venues.narrative: **MG — Sunday 11/22 (AM James & Lex; PM Eva/James & Marcus; entered by Alexis; posted 2:00am ET 11/23)** Net $9,391 vs target $13,967 (67.2%). Morning bar $3,099, evening bar $5,227, Hot Eye $962, Sun Club closed (parts sum to $9,288 vs $9,391 total entered). Food $3,717; no events; comps $198 (2.1%). Guests 214 (115 AM + 99 PM OpenTable); check avg $43.88 (net / guests). Morning: very good Sunday — guests seemed to celebrate the break in the rain after Saturday. Fairly short-staffed all day, but everyone pushed through the rushes; Jack worked the entire restaurant solo through a very busy 10–12, then Carla got rocked 12–2. Great service and happy guests. Evening: busy start and a mellow end, with rushes at 4, 6 and 7; Carla stayed to help through the busy parts. Impressive teamwork and great attitudes. Hot Eye: super slow — a steady first hour, then way down by 9pm; a couple of birthdays and holiday-week guests. Team did much-needed drain cleaning for fruit flies. Kitchen: not a lot going on but a little busier than the average Sunday night; may be out of 12in burrito tortillas, more arriving tomorrow; no other 86s. No events. No incidents. Highlight: D&C superfans stopped by and were amazed by the service and organization of the bar.

venues.name: D&C Seattle
venues.weather: Chilly day, high of 48 and low of 40. Stayed mostly dry until the sun went down and started to drizzle.
venues.narrative: **SEA — Sunday 11/22 (MOD Curtis; entered by Frank; posted 3:50am ET 11/23)** Net $6,415 vs target $7,461 (86.0%). Food $907; no events. Comps $191.92 (2.9%) — a few community members/investors, a few SNDs (lots of celebrations) and a couple of DNLs. 142 guests; check avg $45.18. Sleepy Sunday — no football or major events, so a mellow and smooth service. Main pop came at the beginning of service, then a slow trickle the rest of the night, with a slight uptick in seating in the last couple of hours. Everyone got a break and a bartender was cut early. It was the night before inventory count, so the team got an early start filling cheaters and batches, which allowed closing with two bartenders and a barback. Kitchen: sales were pretty great considering how slow the night was; staff meal was excellent; back to Shigoku oysters. No events; no maintenance needs. 86: St. Germain, Glitterpaw IPA (now Hyperstep West Coast IPA), Monkey 47. Low: Heart of Stone Sour (will be replaced). No incidents; no-shows not charged. Highlight: watching Curtis R&D a new zero-proof cocktail.
